verses.en: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.
verses.pt: Ele: Já cheguei ao meu jardim, minha irmã, minha esposa; colhi minha mirra com minha especiaria; comi meu mel, bebi meu vinho com meu leite. Autor do poema (ou os amigos dos noivos): Comei, amigos; bebei, ó amados, e embebedai-vos.
verses.en_web: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.
verses.en_bbe: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; to take my myrrh with my spice; my wax with my honey; my wine with my milk. Take meat, O friends; take wine, yes, be overcome with love.

verses.en: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.
verses.pt: Ela: Eu estava dormindo, mas meu coração vigiava; era a voz de meu amado, batendo: Abre-me, minha irmã, minha querida, minha pomba, minha perfeita! Porque minha cabeça está cheia de orvalho, meus cabelos das gotas da noite.
verses.en_web: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”
verses.en_bbe: I am sleeping, but my heart is awake; it is the sound of my loved one at the door, saying, Be open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my very beautiful one; my head is wet with dew, and my hair with the drops of the night.

verses.en: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
verses.pt: Já tirei minha roupa; como voltarei a vesti-la? Já lavei meus pés; como vou sujá-los de novo?
verses.en_web: I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?
verses.en_bbe: I have put off my coat; how may I put it on? My feet are washed; how may I make them unclean?

verses.en: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.
verses.pt: Meu amado meteu sua mão pelo buraco da porta,e meu interior se estremeceu por ele.
verses.en_web: My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.
verses.en_bbe: My loved one put his hand on the door, and my heart was moved for him.

verses.en: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
verses.pt: Eu me levantei para abrir a meu amado; minhas mãos gotejavam mirra, e meus dedos derramaram mirra sobre os puxadores da fechadura.
verses.en_web: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
verses.en_bbe: I got up to let my loved one in; and my hands were dropping with myrrh, and my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the lock of the door.

verses.en: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
verses.pt: Eu abri a porta ao meu amado, porém meu amado já tinha saído e ido embora; minha alma como que saía de si por causa de seu falar. Eu o busquei, mas não o achei; eu o chamei, mas ele não me respondeu.
verses.en_web: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left; and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.
verses.en_bbe: I made the door open to my loved one; but my loved one had taken himself away, and was gone, my soul was feeble when his back was turned on me; I went after him, but I did not come near him; I said his name, but he gave me no answer.

verses.en: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
verses.pt: Os guardas que rondavam pela cidade me encontraram; eles me bateram e me feriram; os guardas dos muros tiraram de mim o meu véu.
verses.en_web: The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.
verses.en_bbe: The keepers who go about the town overtook me; they gave me blows and wounds; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

verses.en: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I am sick of love.
verses.pt: Eu vos ordeno, filhas de Jerusalém: jurai que, se achardes o meu amado, dizei a ele que estou doente de amor.
verses.en_web: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love.
verses.en_bbe: I say to you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you see my loved one, what will you say to him? That I am overcome with love.

verses.en: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?
verses.pt: Moças: Ó, tu, mais bela entre as mulheres, como é o teu amado, a quem tu amas mais do que qualquer outro? Como é este teu amado, mais amado que qualquer outro, por quem assim nos mandas jurar?
verses.en_web: How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us?
verses.en_bbe: What is your loved one more than another, O fairest among women? What is your loved one more than another, that you say this to us?

verses.en: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.
verses.pt: Ela: Meu amado é radiante e rosado; ele se destaca entre dez mil.
verses.en_web: My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.
verses.en_bbe: My loved one is white and red, the chief among ten thousand.

verses.en: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.
verses.pt: Sua cabeça é como o mais fino ouro; seus cabelos são crespos, pretos como o corvo.
verses.en_web: His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.
verses.en_bbe: His head is as the most delicate gold; his hair is thick, and black as a raven.

verses.en: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.
verses.pt: Seus olhos são como pombas junto às correntes de águas, lavados em leite, colocados como joias.
verses.en_web: His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.
verses.en_bbe: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the water streams, washed with milk, and rightly placed.

verses.en: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.
verses.pt: As laterais de seu rosto como um canteiro de especiarias, como caixas aromáticas; seus lábios são como lírios, que gotejam fragrante mirra.
verses.en_web: His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
verses.en_bbe: His face is as beds of spices, giving out perfumes of every sort; his lips like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.

verses.en: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.
verses.pt: Suas mãos são como anéis de ouro com pedras de crisólitos; seu abdome como o brilhante marfim, coberto de safiras.
verses.en_web: His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.
verses.en_bbe: His hands are as rings of gold ornamented with beryl-stones; his body is as a smooth plate of ivory covered with sapphires.

verses.en: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
verses.pt: Suas pernas são como colunas de mármore, fundadas sobre bases de ouro puro; seu aspecto é como o Líbano, precioso como os cedros.
verses.en_web: His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
verses.en_bbe: His legs are as pillars of stone on a base of delicate gold; his looks are as Lebanon, beautiful as the cedar-tree.

verses.en: His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.pt: Sua boca é cheia de doçura, e ele é desejável em todos os sentidos; assim é o meu amado; assim é o meu querido, ó filhas de Jerusalém.
verses.en_web: His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.en_bbe: His mouth is most sweet; yes, he is all beautiful. This is my loved one, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
